result:
Since modifying the system PATH requires admin privileges on Windows, here's what you need to do:

**Option 1: Run this command as Administrator (recommended for system-wide PATH)**

Open PowerShell as Administrator and run:
```powershell
$cliPath = "/home/author\.sentinel\bin"
$currentPath = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("PATH", "Machine")
if ($currentPath -notlike "*$cliPath*") {
    [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("PATH", "$cliPath;$currentPath", "Machine")
}
```

**Option 2: Create a symlink in System32 (if you have admin)**

This single command in an admin PowerShell will make `claude` available everywhere:
```powershell
New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path "C:\windows\system32\claude.exe" -Target "/home/author\.sentinel\bin\claude" -Force
```

**Option 3: Set user PATH (affects only current user, no admin needed)**

If you want to set just for the current user without admin:
```powershell
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("PATH", "/home/author\.sentinel\bin;$([Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('PATH', 'User'))", "User")
```

For a true system-wide solution that affects all users and login shells, you'll need to run one of these as Administrator. Would you like me to help with any of these approaches, or do you have admin access to execute one?
